Insidiously effective horror game. The game understands restraint and doesn't show its hand too early. Even when you think you've seen it all, it's inevitable that some new abominable thing will eventually come sprinting and wailing over the hillside, causing all of your group members to collectively scream their lungs out over VOIP.

Also an inherently visceral game. Not only will you grit your teeth and furrow your brow as you slowly hack the island's native population into pieces; you will also stare unhinged at your monitor as you then begin the lengthy procedure of cutting up all of their bodies, cooking, and consuming them. By design, human bodies are the most easily available source of food in The Forest .

Four years in early access, a highly active player-base and enough sales to make it a regular front-page bestsellers fixture on Steam, The Forest has done very well for itself, considering its lengthy public development cycle, and crowded genre. Awesome game!

A pretty fun game if you ask me, it does remind me a lot of tomb raider with the cave exploration and all but also adds it's own feel where important resources are scarce, you have to use everything you have got to kill that mutant to get that special weapon, or you can go home and survive another night and add to your defences. It has a fair few amount of weapons for a game in early access, some need patching up (e.g bow), but the combat feels ok and everything seems to go smoothly. I would like to see a bit more resources to base building rather than just farming logs all day long and maybe a combat feature that would encourage you to be a lot more tactical and block more (parrying, dodging etc.). I haven't noticed any performance issues, authough sometimes when I go into a previous save my food would be gone or something, nothing that breaks the game.

The Forest is a gripping survival horror game that had me hooked. The intelligent enemies and mysterious story kept me on edge throughout. The excessive darkness and server issues were minor setbacks, but the overall experience was totally worth it. Visually stunning and performance-wise solid, it offered an unforgettable adventure. If you're into chills and thrills, give The Forest a shot. You won't be disappointed.

Warning: my experience is basically 100% on a hosted save so it could not fully match Singleplayer/Server experiences.

The idea of the game is fun but the game itself has so many underlying issues it gets procedurally frustrating and taxing the more you play it, feeling like a beta on which teh devs wrote "1.0" and called it a day.

- Caves are too important. Maps, tools, weapons are mostly, if not only, found in caves with no way, but an online map, to understand which is an "early game" cave and which contains every single enemy in the game. Currently, I'm 12 hours in a save, with pickaxe, modern axe, rebreather.. but no map nor goggles to actually see underwater.

- It's extremely glitchy. Hitting a prop (shark corpse, stalagmite, anything) can propel you in air, resulting in fall damages, or enemies charge into walls, reappear somewhere else and hit you anyway.
Hell we lost a house because a crawling enemy flipped the log sled which hit the building and deleted it.

- Lacks basic things that were already common when the game came out. Most of the items you collect will permanently remain in the inventory because of the lack of boxes or other storage facilities. No way to drop or trade bar with the tin box.

+ Despite being basically throwing everything you have at the enemy, fights are fun.

+ Boats.

No idea how this game has the positive hype it has...

Every single system in this game is sub-par, buggy, unfun.

Combat is jank.
Building is pointless.
AI is TERRIBLE, they either run in circles right next to you, or run at you (and miss) on repeat.
There are literally only 5 different enemy types (other than reskins).
Cave exploration is interesting... the first time, tedious after the 3rd-7th identically uninspired scenes.
Food/Drink system is pointless, every 2nd cave room drops 10 sodas and 10 candy bars, never need to cook/prep food.
Get ready to spend 2 minutes after EVERY encounter burning bodies to rebuild your armour.

I've played the game before in my friends account, but DAMN the game is amazing! The music is a bit loud and you sometimes get jumpscared. Multiplayer is made pretty well if don't mind some bugs. Playing singleplayer for the first 20 hours will be like in a horror game, but after that you'll get used to it and instead of Cannibals trying to kill you. You will be clapping their cheeks. The Story is not forced on you in neither Singleplayer or Multiplayer. You can play if you want to, but you can also just survive and build a base. In total I've got over 150 hours and I still quite enjoy the game so I'll think you will too.

TL:DR
Game is made really well, music sometimes is a bit loud, but I think you'll really like it. If you and your friends decide to play together, DO IT! It's very fun!

V1.0 Update : "Log sled built now has set flag color that can’t be changed to help identify its location "
Before, there was a flag when built, and we could manually set the color to an other or even delete it. Now we can't, our screen is full of pink flags for every little log sled we build. Also, log sleds are properly unbreakable, bomb, burn, cut, smash, nothing work.
How can that be an improvment? An update isn't supposed to make the game better, with more options than before?
Really it was way more immersive when we could make all these flags invisible.
Please come back to the previous log sled settings, the ones where we had the choice.

Oh wow, what a journey. I finally got a gaming PC again and thought I'd pick things up with gaming with my brother. Not being very good at first person shooters I've preferred to play some type of co-op with him. Did a bit of research and this came up high on the list. It was a blast the whole way through. We died a lot in the beginning, but after figuring out a few things (I don't know why we didn't think to build mass armor) things got a lot easier from there.

The game is definitely scary at first, and I personally needed to refer to the wiki. Since this is a non-linear type game you might have to go back if you miss something, which happened to use a few times but it wasn't unbearably annoying. It was cool that there was an alternate ending, too. Now that I'm done I'm not sure if there will be a lot of replayability, but I definitely feel like I got my money's worth. Now to find another co-op...

One last thing to mention: the last game that reminded me most of this as a FPS survival horror type game was System Shock 2, which I also played with my bro. The only thing I would've loved to take from SS2 would've been the RPG system, but the balance is still well done so no complaints.

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (95%): many reviews praise the co-op and the story.
Bugs and crashes are the most common complaint by far.

details.text: Complaints about bugs and crashes are much rarer in recent reviews, at 7% against 25% across all reviews.
Players in their first two hours are the least positive group, while those past 50 hours are the most positive.
